title: draw_ring_segments does not validate segs values against the table bounds
detail: New shared proc indexes SPAWN_RING_TABLE with unvalidated runtime slice values. A seg outside [0, SPAWN_RING_SEGS) hits the bounds check (or reads garbage with -no-bounds-check); no guard exists.
recommended_fix: Guard at proc entry (e.g. `if i < 0 || i >= SPAWN_RING_SEGS { continue }`) or accept a fixed-size enumeration type so out-of-range segments fail fast.

title: palcheck section 5 discards lookup/edit error results; index-0 fallback can silently degrade the fixture
evidence:
res, _ := pp.node_type_index(cat, "residential")
host, _ := pp.node_type_index(cat, "content_host")
rtm, _ := pp.node_type_index(cat, "router_mid")
narrow, _ := pp.pipe_tier_index(cat, "narrow")
...
pp.topology_apply_edit(&state.topology, pp.Command{kind = pp.Cmd_Draw_Pipe{a = n0, b = n1, tier = narrow}}, cat)  // result discarded x3
// core/catalog.odin:1506-1511 failure contract: returns 0, false
detail: node_type_index/pipe_tier_index return (0, false) on miss and topology_apply_edit returns an Edit_Error — all discarded. A catalog token rename silently spawns type/tier 0 nodes or drops an edge; the ECMP check only catches some degradations.
recommended_fix: Check each discarded bool/Edit_Error (fmt.eprintfln + fails += 1, like the load_frame path) so fixture lookups degrade loudly instead of falling back to index 0.
